name: Biscuits - Glucose
description: Plain, lightly sweet glucose biscuits, the everyday tea-time biscuit in most Karnataka homes and dunked in chai or coffee. A 300 g pack keeps a family in biscuits for about a week and is the size usually kept in the kitchen tin.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 (pro-rata estimate: Parle-G 800 g pouch MRP ₹100 on zepto.com / bigbasket, 250 g pack retails about ₹30)
notes: Image is the Parle-G 300 g export pack (English/French label) - the only 300 g front shot on Open Food Facts; landscape framing. Store should confirm whether it stocks Parle-G 250 g or a 300 g pack.

name: Biscuits - Marie
description: Thin, crisp, mildly sweet Marie biscuits that are served with tea and coffee across Karnataka and are the usual biscuit offered to guests. A 250 g family pack holds about 45 biscuits, a week or so of tea-time for a small household.
notes: Photo is the Britannia Marie Gold 250 g pack; slightly soft focus and landscape framing, but it is the exact pack size.

name: Biscuits - Cream
description: Sandwich biscuits with a sweet cream filling, most often chocolate (bourbon) or vanilla and orange. A 150 g sleeve is the standard pocket-money pack picked up for school tiffins and evening tea in Karnataka homes.
mrp_source: https://blinkit.com/prn/britannia-bourbon-the-original-biscuit/prid/263544 (Britannia Bourbon 150 g, MRP ₹35; bigbasket lists the same pack at MRP ₹40, Sept 2026 search)
notes: Image is the Parle Fab! Bourbon 150 g sleeve (portrait, sharp) - Open Food Facts has no clean Britannia Bourbon 150 g front shot. Parle now sells this line as Hide & Seek Bourbon; either brand is stocked in Karnataka kiranas.

name: Rusk
description: Twice-baked slices of sweet bread, crisp and dry, usually with a hint of cardamom or sooji. Rusk is dunked in tea or coffee in the morning and evening; a 300 g pack holds about 25 to 30 slices and lasts a small family a week or two.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 (bigbasket lists Britannia Toastea Premium Bake Rusk 273-300 g at ₹42 offer price: https://www.bigbasket.com/pd/312568/britannia-toastea-premium-bake-rusk-with-goodness-of-elaichi-sooji-wheat-273-g/ ; 668 g pack MRP ₹140 on blinkit)
notes: Photo is a Britannia Toastea rusk pack shot on a shop shelf (other packs visible in the background, portrait framing). Britannia's Indian rusk pack is 273 g nominal, sold as the '300 g' size; Parle Rusk and local bakery rusk are the alternatives.

name: Namkeen Mixture
description: Savoury snack mix of fried sev, boondi, peanuts, flattened rice and dal, spiced and salted. Mixture is the standard evening snack with coffee in Karnataka and is put out for guests; a 200 g pouch fills a snack bowl three or four times.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 (Haldiram's Navratan Mix 200 g: blinkit ₹50, flipkart ₹57, Wellness Forever MRP ₹65 - https://blinkit.com/prn/haldirams-navratan-mixture-namkeen/prid/19297)
notes: Photo is the Haldiram's Navratan Mix 200 g pouch (portrait, clear). Local Karnataka-style mixture from a Hospet bakery or a regional brand may be what the store actually stocks.

name: Potato Chips
description: Thin fried potato crisps in a foil pack, sold in salted, masala and chilli-lime flavours. The 52 g pack is the twenty-rupee size that goes into school bags and bus journeys and is enough for one or two people.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 (Lay's 48-55 g packs are the ₹20 price point in India; pack weight varies by flavour and promotion)
notes: Photo is the Lay's Chile Limon ₹20 pack (55 g) on a plain background; the Magic Masala flavour sells more but its Open Food Facts photos are hand-held ₹10 packs. Image width 788 px.

name: Noodles
description: Instant masala noodles: a dried noodle cake with a spice sachet, ready in a couple of minutes on the stove. The 70 g single pack makes one bowl and is a common quick breakfast or after-school snack, often cooked with chopped onion, tomato and green chilli.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 (Maggi 2-Minute Masala single 70 g pack has been MRP ₹14 since 2022; 4 x 70 g multipack MRP ₹56 on flipkart/blinkit)
notes: Photo is the Maggi 2-Minute Noodles Masala 70 g single pack, portrait, clear. Yippee (Sunfeast) is the usual second brand on Karnataka shelves.

name: Vermicelli
description: Thin wheat-semolina noodles, called shavige in Kannada, cooked into shavige upma or bath for breakfast and into sweet payasa (kheer) for festivals. A 400 g pack gives four to five family breakfasts and keeps for months in the tin.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 (Bambino plain vermicelli 400 g lists at MRP ₹46-65 in zeptonow.com / blinkit.com search snippets; the roasted 425 g pack is ₹76 at https://www.bigbasket.com/pd/40086008/bambino-vermicelli-roasted-400-g/)
notes: Image is the Bambino Everyday Essentials plain vermicelli 425 g pack (the nearest pack size on Open Food Facts; India listing), portrait framing, slight glare. MTR and Anil are the other vermicelli brands seen on Karnataka shelves; store should confirm plain vs roasted and 400 vs 425 g.

name: Onion
description: Red onions, called eerulli in Kannada, the base of almost every Karnataka curry, sambar, upma and chutney and eaten raw with meals. A 1 kg pack is about six to eight medium onions, enough for a small family for four or five days.
mrp_source: https://market.todaypricerates.com/Bangalore-vegetables-price-in-Karnataka (Bangalore retail onion ₹63-74/kg on 05 Sep 2026; loose produce, price moves weekly)
notes: Portrait photo of red onions in crates at Koyambedu market, Chennai; matches the Indian red onion sold in Hospet.

name: Potato
description: Potatoes, aloogadde in Kannada, go into palya (dry curry), sagu for poori and dosa, bonda and vegetable sambar. A 1 kg pack is about seven to nine medium potatoes and keeps for two weeks in a cool, dark corner of the kitchen.
mrp_source: https://market.todaypricerates.com/Bangalore-vegetables-price-in-Karnataka (Bangalore retail potato ₹34-40/kg on 05 Sep 2026; loose produce, price moves weekly)
notes: Landscape photo of potatoes in a basket at Koyambedu market, Chennai; item fills the frame so it crops to square cleanly.

name: Tomato
description: Ripe red tomatoes, tomato or tomyato in Kannada, used daily in rasam, sambar, tomato bath, gojju and chutney. A 1 kg pack is roughly eight to twelve tomatoes, about a week's cooking for a small family, best used within four or five days.
mrp_source: https://market.todaypricerates.com/Bangalore-vegetables-price-in-Karnataka (Bangalore retail tomato ₹30-35/kg on 05 Sep 2026; loose produce, price swings sharply with season)
notes: Landscape photo of tomatoes in blue crates at Koyambedu market, Chennai; crops to square well.

name: Green Chilli
description: Fresh green chillies, hasi menasinakayi in Kannada, slit or chopped into the tadka for upma, palya, chutney and sambar, and eaten whole with meals. A 250 g pack holds around 30 to 40 chillies, enough for a small family for a week or two if kept in the fridge.
mrp_source: https://market.todaypricerates.com/Bangalore-vegetables-price-in-Karnataka (Bangalore retail green chilli ₹75-88/kg on 05 Sep 2026, so about ₹19-22 per 250 g; loose produce)
notes: Near-square top-down photo of a heap of thin green chillies at an Indian market.

name: Ginger
description: Fresh ginger root, shunti in Kannada, grated into chai, ground with garlic into the paste for curries and biryani, and used in chutneys and rasam. A 250 g pack is a few large pieces, about two to three weeks of daily use for a small family.
mrp_source: https://market.todaypricerates.com/Bangalore-vegetables-price-in-Karnataka (Bangalore retail ginger ₹139-164/kg on 05 Sep 2026, so about ₹35-41 per 250 g; loose produce)
notes: Portrait styled flat-lay of fresh ginger on a wooden board, with lime halves and ginger powder at the edges; the two plain rhizome photos on Commons (sprouting rhizomes) were rejected as not grocery-like.

name: Garlic
description: Whole garlic bulbs, bellulli in Kannada, crushed into the tadka for dal and sambar, pounded into ginger-garlic paste, and roasted for chutney pudi. A 250 g pack is about eight to twelve bulbs and keeps for a month in a dry, airy basket.
mrp_source: https://market.todaypricerates.com/Bangalore-vegetables-price-in-Karnataka (Bangalore retail garlic ₹253-299/kg on 05 Sep 2026, so about ₹63-75 per 250 g; loose produce)
notes: Landscape photo of garlic bulbs in a basket at Salem market, Tamil Nadu; South Indian garlic type, crops to square well.

name: Coriander Leaves
description: Fresh coriander, kothambari soppu in Kannada, chopped over sambar, rasam, upma and bisi bele bath just before serving, and ground into green chutney. One bunch is about 100 g and covers two or three days of garnishing; wrap it in a cloth or paper in the fridge to keep it fresh.
mrp_source: https://market.todaypricerates.com/Bangalore-vegetables-price-in-Karnataka (Bangalore retail coriander leaves ₹19-22 on 05 Sep 2026; loose produce, bunch price in Hospet is usually ₹10-20)
notes: Landscape photo of tied coriander bunches on a dark table; only clearly-licensed bunch photo found on Commons.

name: Curry Leaves
description: Fresh curry leaves, karibevu in Kannada, dropped into hot oil at the start of almost every Karnataka dish, from sambar and rasam to upma, palya and chitranna. One bunch is a handful of sprigs, enough for a week of daily tadka, and the leaves keep well in a paper-lined box in the fridge.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 (a bunch of curry leaves sells for ₹5-10 at Karnataka vegetable shops; Bangalore retail listed at ₹50-59 on 05 Sep 2026 at https://market.todaypricerates.com/Bangalore-vegetables-price-in-Karnataka, which reads as a per-kg rate)
notes: Single curry-leaf sprig on a white background with a small '10 cm' scale bar in the top right; landscape. Two other Commons candidates were rejected (growing plant with busy background; photographer watermark).

name: Banana
description: Ripe yellow bananas, balehannu in Kannada, eaten as an everyday fruit, offered at pooja, and mashed into rasayana and sheera. A pack of six covers a small family for two or three days; the small elakki type and the larger pachbale are both common in Hospet.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 (pachbale/robusta bananas sell for about ₹50-60 a dozen and elakki for ₹80-100 a dozen in Karnataka towns, so six pieces run ₹25-50; Bangalore retail list at https://market.todaypricerates.com/Bangalore-vegetables-price-in-Karnataka shows only raw plantain at ₹14-17)
notes: Portrait photo of ripe yellow banana bunches on the stalk at Koyambedu market, Chennai; the Malleswaram (Bangalore) market photo on Commons was rejected as unripe and blemished.

name: Lemon
description: Small, juicy lemons, nimbehannu in Kannada, squeezed over rasam, chitranna (lemon rice), pickled whole, and stirred into nimbe sharbat on hot days. A pack of four covers a small family for about a week and keeps well at room temperature.
mrp_source: typical shelf price, Sept 2026 (lemons sell at about ₹5-8 apiece in Karnataka towns, so four pieces run ₹20-30; Bangalore retail lemon listed at ₹55-65 on 05 Sep 2026 at https://market.todaypricerates.com/Bangalore-vegetables-price-in-Karnataka)
notes: Studio photo of a whole and a halved yellow lemon on black; this is the larger European lemon rather than the small round green-yellow Indian nimbe. Commons candidates for the Indian type were all on-tree or market scenes dominated by flowers, so this clean shot was preferred; landscape framing.
